newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks led to higher close by pharma shares.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks led to higher close by pharma shares.

text.p: ZURICH, July 14 - Swiss shares put an end to last week's three-day correction and closed higher, buoyed by firmer pharmaceutical shares.
However, the market ended below the day's highs as some investors continued to take profits, one dealer said.
One trader said the outlook was mixed. "In July, we could see a see-saw bourse with the SMI ranging from 5,700 to 6,000," he said, referring to the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
He said fundamentals such as the strong dollar were positive. "But technically speaking, the situation looks shaky," he added.
SMI rose 44.3 points or 0.76 percent to 5,845.8 after hitting a day's high at 5,892.7 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 22.59 points or 0.62 percent to 3,683.8 points.
"We had less volume than on previous days and activity was less hectic," one dealer said. Bourse volume stood at 2.44 billion Swiss francs.
Pharma and life sciences giant Novartis registered shares led the actives list, adding 38 francs to 2,409.
Roche certificates added 110 francs to 1,285. Roche said it would release sales figures for the first half-year on Tuesday before bourse opening.
Insurer Winterthur jumped 56 francs or 3.95 percent to 1,474. The share was helped by vague takeover speculation after two big shareholders made their stakes public last Friday.

Maverick Swiss financier Martin Ebner's BZ Group has 18.3 percent of Winterthur, with another five percent placed with customers of his BZ Bank, while Swiss Re holds around five percent. Ebner said in a weekend interview he could not rule out some group taking over Winterthur.

Shares of medical technology maker Sulzer Medica, sold by parent Sulzer AG in an IPO, closed the first day of trading at 408 francs, above an issue price of 350 francs. The high was an opening 440 francs, the low at 405.
